analysis:
All three changed files are test-only: GenerationLoopExitThinkingServingTests.swift and GenerationLoopExitThinkingTests.swift (added) and MiMoV26EncodedMediaIngressTests.swift (modified). No production source, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, authorization or cache-storage code changes in the supplied evidence, so none of the TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 or TB-011 controls are weakened. I found no secrets, network calls, file writes or privilege use in the tests.

The new tests exercise a loop-guard "exit thinking" feature (GenerationLoopExitThinking and GenerationLoopExitThinkingPolicy) that is implemented in production source outside this batch. They show its intended behavior. It is default-on for gemma4 model types. It is disabled when logprobs are requested, when the close marker is missing from the tokenizer, and when a tool call is seen. Env override DARKBLOOM_LOOP_EXIT_THINKING is passed through LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys. On a detected loop the guard cancels the row and the bridge submits a continuation whose prompt is the original prompt plus all generated tokens plus the close marker. The next review pass should check the production side, which is unseen here. Open questions:
- The continuation re-submits generated tokens as a new prompt. Does it keep the same cacheSalt and cache scope, with no cross-account prefix-cache reuse (T-041)?
- Are usage and billing token counts correct?
- Do the continuation's maxTokens bounds hold?
- Are slot and KV reservations released through waitForRowRelease?

The MiMo test change replaces a polling loop with a hook-driven expectation (setMediaReservationRemovalHookForTesting, EventCounter). It still asserts that managedMediaReservationCountForTesting == 0. The hook is a test-only API whose production definition is outside this batch; confirm it is not reachable or compiled in release builds.

No findings. Production behavior of the loop-exit feature was not available for review.
